notes.notes:
Patch notes vol 1.1

- Bug fixes with bounces that caused to loose player control
- Fixed issues with some achievements

We're slowly working to make Mexico, 1921: A Deep Slumber to be a better experience. All your reviews and comments are very important to us.

With love,
Mácula Interactive.

notes.title: Patch 1.
notes.notes:
Patch notes vol.1

- Fixed an issue with the object "task list" that could block you from the final cinematic of that level.
- Fixed issues with gallery photo display in the notebook 
- Adjusted some minor issues with the camera tutorial that might make it smoother
- Fixed rotating issue with the archive's newspapers from The Unilateral.
- Fixed some code in the notebook descriptions and some typos. 
- Better scrolling feature for glossary and notebook.
- Fixed loading issue with floor in National Palace main patio.
- started replacing some animations for more "natural" ones.
- Fixed some continuity issues in cinematics.

We're slowly working to make Mexico, 1921: A Deep Slumber to be a better experience. All your reviews and comments are very important to us.

With love,
Mácula Interactive.

notes.title: SPANISH stream of Mexico, 1921: A Deep Slumber
notes.notes:
For the first time, join us in a Spanish-language broadcast to explore a fragment of Mexico, 1921: A Deep Dream with Daniel and Eduardo, our team of animators.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501761/65ce46cbe5ec5c16dee1ec95284948a0defcd90c.png[/img]

For the Mácula Interactive team it has been a long road and we are very excited to finally share with you the result of several years of effort and love.

Welcome to posrevolutionary Mexico.

Love,

notes.title: Launch date for Mexico, 1921: A Deep Slumber
notes.notes:
We're very excited to finally announce that our historical narrative adventure game, [i]Mexico, 1921. A Deep Slumber[/i] will release on [b]September 13 on Steam[/b],  just in time for Mexican Independence Day and Hispanic Heritage Month.

https://youtu.be/r0rtt06hjoM?si=4pgWwZhbfY6hftEW

We've built an interdisciplinary team that includes historians, cultural managers, filmmakers, and of course, artists, programmers and animators to build what we believe is an interactive archive of Mexican history. Walk through real places in Mexico City and interact with historical documents and characters. Through the life of Juan Aguirre, a young photojournalist you’ll be swept into the transformation of Mexico with the turn of the century and uncover a mystery: Who planned the assassination of President Álvaro Obregón?

To celebrate our launch date we want to share some of our concept art from our archive!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501761/36b739317fcf23bb9b76cd58988a75b7ffcde22e.png[/img]
[i]One of our early concepts for Juan, Archivero and Pelón.[/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501761/6f8fad7328c41f89eb9a3eeeadfddd3790dbbaf4.png[/img]
[i]First concept from Archivero.[/i]

Thank you to everyone who's been following our journey, thank you for your support and patience, we're very happy you're here.

You can play our demo now and get ready for September 13th!

Love,
Mácula Interactive.

notes.title: Next Fest Demo Stream!
notes.notes:
Join Paola Vera, Mácula's Director for a full demo gameplay commentary stream! 

In this demo for Mexico, 1921 a Deep Slumber, you play a short prologue through the eyes of Inspector Roberto Cruz, the first night after the assassination of President Álvaro Obregón in 1928.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501761/ea89cb902a26c633ecff87ed261a801fce181e4c.png[/img]

After that, you’re Juan Aguirre, standing on Mexico City's main square on your first assignment as a reporter for the underground newspaper "El Contracorriente". Get a glimpse of the art style and main mechanics like Juan’s nosey mode, camera and notebook.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42501761/18593aa27959f76e9255aa0c577ae407f1d58aa6.png[/img]

This first update prepared for Next Fest features an updated Nosey mode and Camera UI as well as sound balance update and some minor fixes for performance and text display.

Welcome to post revolutionary Mexico City!
